newsitem.title: KENYA: Burundi, Zaire refugees arrested in Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Burundi, Zaire refugees arrested in Tanzania.

text.p: Tanzanian authorities have arrested 360 refugees from Burundi and Zaire in a crackdown in the western town of Kigoma, state radio reported on Wednesday.

Radio Tanzania, monitored in the Kenyan capital Nairobi by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted Kigoma regional commissioner Alhaji Ahmed Lugusha as saying some of those arrested in the Monday operation had been ordered back to Zaire.
Lugusha said nine Tanzanians were also arrested for illegally harbouring refugees in their houses, and were expected to appear in court soon, according to the radio.

Senior Rwandan government officials said last weekend that all Rwandan refugees who had fled to Tanzania in 1994 -- estimated by the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR at 540,000 -- had returned to their homeland by December 28.

However, thousands of Burundian refugees and scores of Zaireans remain in Tanzania and it is not yet known whether Tanzanian authorities will force them out in the same style as they did the refugees from Rwanda.
